title: Yara and the Witness
premise: When a drowned man washes up in the flooded quarry wearing clothes stolen from Rafael Dunmore's own closet, the town of Halloway assumes it's a cruel prank—until Rafael recognizes the dead man as Tommy Vess, the boy who vanished twenty years ago, the case Rafael's perfect memory has never let him forget. As Rafael investigates, he realizes his photographic recall holds fragments of that night he was made to forget: his father, the town's beloved sheriff, was there, and so were half the men who now run Halloway. The witness everyone protected wasn't Rafael—it was Yara, the foster girl who lived with them, whose testimony was buried to save the town's reputation. Racing against the killer, who is eliminating everyone who remembers, Rafael must reconstruct the truth from memory alone and choose between exposing his own family or letting the past stay drowned. In the end, Rafael testifies alongside Yara, toppling the town's power structure at the cost of his name, his job, and his carefully alphabetized invisibility—and finds in Yara the family he never actually had.
about_author: Jonah Ashgrove is the pen name of a former small-town court reporter who spent a decade transcribing other people's secrets before writing them into fiction. He lives somewhere in the Appalachian foothills with two dogs and an unhealthy interest in cold cases.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Towns
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. We meet Rafael filing insurance claims in Halloway, establishing his photographic memory and his philosophy of invisible living. A routine flood-damage claim takes him past the old quarry. Emotional beat: quiet unease—the sense that order is a kind of hiding.

chapters.title: A Body Wearing My Life
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The drowned man pulled from the quarry wears Rafael's missing gray coat and watch. Police dismiss it as theft, but Rafael recognizes the face: Tommy Vess, missing since 2005. Beat: shock cracking open twenty years of careful silence.

chapters.title: Everyone Swore It Was Closed
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael digs out his memory of the original case file—ruled accidental drowning, no body ever found. The current sheriff, Dale Pruitt, urges him to let it go. Beat: first brush with institutional pressure.

chapters.title: Yara
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Introduce Yara Okafor, now a hospice nurse two states away, who left Halloway at nineteen and never looked back. She sees news of the body online and burns her toast staring at Rafael's name. Beat: dread and unfinished grief.

chapters.title: What the Coat Remembers
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael examines the stolen clothes and realizes details only someone inside his house could have known—the mended cuff, the hidden spare key. Someone from that year is sending him a message. Beat: paranoia taking root.

chapters.title: The Men Who Run Halloway
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael maps the town's power web: Judge Ellery Crane, bank owner Walt Meechum, Pastor Deke Sorrell—all present at the quarry the summer Tommy died. His own father, Sheriff Frank Dunmore, closed the case in nine days. Beat: dawning horror about his father.

chapters.title: A Letter Twenty Years Late
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara receives an unsigned letter: 'They know you remember.' She drives back toward Halloway against every instinct. Flashback to her arrival as a foster child in the Dunmore house. Beat: reluctant homecoming.

chapters.title: Fragments of That Night
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael interrogates his own memory—flashes of headlights, his father's muddy boots, Yara crying on the porch—but the middle of the night is strangely smooth, like a page torn out. He suspects he was drugged. Beat: violation of the one thing he trusted, his mind.

chapters.title: The Reunion
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Rafael and Yara meet at the diner; twenty years of distance collapse into wary alliance. She reveals she saw something that night but was coached by Frank Dunmore into silence. Beat: fragile trust, two witnesses reassembling.

chapters.title: Walt Meechum Drowns
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Before they can interview him, banker Walt Meechum is found dead in his bathtub—officially a heart attack. Rafael notices water in lungs that shouldn't be there. Beat: the killer is ahead of them, and the pattern is murder dressed as accident.

chapters.title: Sheriff Pruitt's Warning
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Sheriff Pruitt corners Yara, offering money and a bus ticket, then threatening a fabricated drug charge. She records the conversation on her phone. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: My Father's Locked Drawer
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael breaks into his late father's preserved study and finds a locked drawer, inside: Tommy Vess's real autopsy photos, never filed, and a cashier's check signed by Crane. Beat: betrayal made physical—his father bought the cover-up.

chapters.title: The Night I Can't See
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Under Yara's prompting, Rafael reconstructs the erased hours: his father dosed his root beer to keep him asleep while the men met Tommy at the quarry. Yara, fourteen, watched from the tree line. Beat: grief for the boy Rafael was.

chapters.title: Pastor Sorrell Confesses Halfway
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Dying pastor Deke Sorrell admits the men paid Tommy off after he witnessed Crane's hit-and-run that killed a migrant worker—but insists 'no one meant for the boy to go in the water.' Then Sorrell's oxygen line is tampered with. Beat: partial truth, rising body count.

chapters.title: They Come for Yara
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara's motel room is ransacked; her recording survives on a cloud backup. She goes dark, sheltering with Rafael. In the close quarters, their found-family bond from childhood resurfaces. Beat: tenderness under siege.

chapters.title: Judge Crane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Crane offers Rafael everything: his father's reputation restored posthumously, a judgeship, wealth—if he declares the deaths natural and burns the photos. Rafael, tempted by the return of his ordered life, refuses. Beat: the corruption theme crystallized in one offer.

chapters.title: The Quarry at Low Water
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Drought lowers the quarry; the pair find Tommy's bicycle and a second set of remains—the migrant worker, Marco Reyes, never reported missing. Physical proof linking both deaths. Beat: grim vindication, the drowned past surfacing literally.

chapters.title: Pruitt Breaks
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Confronted with the recording and the remains, Sheriff Pruitt confesses he helped stage the 2005 ruling as a young deputy and names Crane's fixer: Rafael's own cousin, Nate Dunmore—the man who stole the clothes to force the truth open. Beat: the message-sender revealed, motives tangled with loyalty.

chapters.title: Nate's War
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Nate, wracked with guilt, explains he staged the body to reignite the case when Crane moved to demolish the quarry and bury evidence forever. But Crane has taken Nate hostage at the courthouse. Beat: ally turned leverage, clock running out.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: Climax, dual POV. At an emergency hearing packed with the town, Rafael delivers a flawless eyewitness reconstruction from memory—every detail timestamped—while Yara plays the recording and identifies Crane at the quarry. Crane lunges, is arrested; Nate is wounded protecting them. Beat: memory as weapon, courage over invisibility.

chapters.title: After the Verdict
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Trials conclude; the town convulses—jobs lost, names cleared, Marco Reyes finally mourned. Rafael resigns from insurance, unsure who he is without secrets to file. Beat: disorientation before rebirth.

chapters.title: Yara and the Witness
chapters.summary: Dual POV closing. Rafael and Yara reopen the Dunmore house as a cold-case resource center, the drawer's contents donated to the state. On the quarry rim, renamed for Tommy and Marco, they scatter flowers. Beat: resolution—found family, truth survived, and a man finally visible.
